Subject: Sudden drop in quality for promptset B in our A/B (Q4 campaign)

Marcus / Laura —

Quick heads-up: during today's morning ramp for our Q4 promotion, we saw a clear degradation on Promptset B (the variant Redwood recommended). The A/B shows a ~12% drop in helpfulness score and multiple hallucination cases in the same content slice (billing/instructions). We've attached our export (small sample + metrics) — label: praxis_eval_report_v2.pdf.

Impact: ~18% of live impressions tied to the variant; client stakeholders are already seeing noisy outputs. Can you confirm whether there were any model/quantization changes, routing changes, or prompttemplate updates on your side between 02/19–02/21? We need a triage plan and an ETA for mitigation; customer is asking whether we should pause the A/B.

Thanks — appreciate quick confirmation.

Erin Walsh

Erin.Walsh@praxishealth.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Walsh <erin@praxishealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Sudden drop in quality for promptset B in our A/B (Q4 campaign)

Erin — thanks for the flag and the report. We're looking into this now. Quick answers up front: no deliberate model change was rolled to production from our staged lanes between 02/19–02/21, and there were no quantization jobs in that window. That said, routing and cache behavior can surface variance; well triage with logs and cached prefixes.

Immediate plan (owners & timeline):
- Grace: run the differential eval & slice analysis on the attached sample + the live logs (ETA 4 hours).
- Dev: prepare a rollback/canary script for promptset B to switch to the pinned variant (v20271203) and a fallback route to promptset A if latency/quality worsens (ETA 6 hours).
- Laura: coordinate comm to Praxis and procure an interim status + ask for any additional failing examples (ETA 2 hours).

Acceptance criteria for us to re-open the A/B (proposed):
1) differential helpfulness delta <= 1.5% (B vs A) on the flagged slice;
2) hallucination incidents reduced to <2 per 1000 requests;
3) no upstream latency increase > 10ms p95 vs current baseline.

I'll treat this as P1 for the next 24 hours. Grace/Dev — please drop status updates to this thread and post to PRA-1423. Erin — we'll share interim artifacts to the Eval dashboard link once available.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus / Erin — I've started the slice-level diff against the Eval dashboard (link: https://evals.redwood.ai/dashboards/praxis/ab-run-2028-02-20). Early signal: the regressions concentrate on templates that contain multi-step billing instructions and numeric tables. Possible vectors: recent prompttemplate normalization (whitespace/linebreak changes) or subtle temperature drift on the serving side due to a misapplied runtime override.

What I'll run now (ETA ~3h):
- full slice diff (helpfulness, correctness, hallucination rate) by template and customer segment;
- token-level KL drift check for the model variants used in the A/B;
- KV cache hit/miss correlation for the prefixes that map to the billing slice.

Proposed short-term acceptance gating (for internal rollback decision):
- If B's hallucination rate > 5x A in the billing slice => immediate pause of B for that slice and fallback to A (automated route).
- If diff helpfulness > 5% for the flagged slice => pause B globally for Praxis until corrected.

I'll upload the analysis CSV and a short write-up to PRA-1423 and attach the session logs we pulled.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior ML Engineer, Inference Quality
Redwood Inference
